title: Ethiopian Chickpea Stew
community: All of Ethiopia — the whole chickpea fasting stew
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Shimbra Wat — whole chickpeas slow-cooked in a berbere sauce with onion, garlic, and tomato. The whole-chickpea fasting stew — more textured than Shiro Wat (which uses chickpea flour), with the chickpeas providing a pleasing firmness in the sauce.
longDesc: Shimbra Wat uses whole chickpeas where Shiro uses chickpea flour — the result is a stew with distinct texture, the chickpeas holding their shape in the berbere sauce. It requires pre-soaking and longer cooking but rewards with a more satisfying texture.
steps: Boil soaked chickpeas 45 minutes until tender (or pressure cook 25 minutes).
Add oil and berbere. Fry 3 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, tomatoes. Cook 5 minutes.
Add cooked chickpeas and their liquid.
Simmer 15—20 minutes until sauce is thick.
chefTips: Pre-soak 12 hours — reduces cooking time significantly.
The chickpea cooking liquid adds body to the sauce — use it.
commonMistakes: Not soaking — very long cooking time.
cookingScience: Chickpea starch partially dissolves into the cooking liquid during the long boiling — this starchy liquid is used as the sauce base, naturally thickening without added starch.
sustainabilityTips: Chickpeas fix atmospheric nitrogen — improve soil fertility as they grow.
culturalNote: Shimbra Wat is the textured fasting stew — where Shiro is smooth and Misir Wat is silky, Shimbra provides the satisfying bite of whole chickpeas. Together they demonstrate the remarkable textural variety of Ethiopian legume cooking.
